newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sandinistas seek talks to ease post-vote tensions.
newsitem.headline: Sandinistas seek talks to ease post-vote tensions.

text.p: Nicaragua's left-wing Sandinista Front called on Tuesday for a "national dialogue" to reach agreement in the highly polarised country after losing a bitter election.
Former President Daniel Ortega, the Sandinista leader, repeated his position that Nicaragua's Oct. 20 vote was fraudulent and had led to a political crisis threatening stability.

But he told a news conference, "The Sandinista Front is aware of the responsibility it has and calls for the immediate start of a national dialogue to set the basis for the governability of the country."

He presented a 14-point plan that included calls for mutual respect among political parties, an end to political confrontation, reform of the electoral law, and respect for the armed forces and current property laws.
Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance defeated Ortega 51 percent to 38 percent and will be sworn in as president on Jan. 10.
